messages:
Alex: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a path for the API compatibility work. Do we consolidate the various shims into a single lightweight 'compat' layer, or prune the surface and force clients to migrate? Tradeoffs: short-term customer UX vs long-term runtime/maintenance cost.
Maria: Short answer: consolidation buys us time but increases runtime complexity and test surface. Pruning is cleaner long term but will create migration pain.
Kevin: Can we quantify the maintenance delta? Right now we have duplicated header/handshake logic across ingress, gateway, and the SDK adapters. That duplication is the main culprit.
Jin: Telemetry angle — if we consolidate we should instrument client-version and route usage so we can identify cohorts that haven't migrated. That supports an automated nudging strategy.
Sam: From infra perf tests: adding an extra proxy/layer without optimizing batching adds ~6-12ms p99 on our staging load. That's measurable for latency-sensitive customers.
Alex: Good to know. Another axis: developer experience. A single compat shim reduces support tickets in the near term. Pruning forces customers to update SDKs and may spike support.
Maria: My proposal: a hybrid 3-phase plan. 1) Consolidate current translators into a single lightweight shim behind a feature flag. 2) Run shadow-prune testing + telemetry for 6 weeks to validate behavior. 3) Announce and remove the shim with an 8-week deprecation window for tenants not opted into extended support.
Kevin: I like the hybrid idea but want a strict rule set for the shim: it should only do canonical transformations (envelope/header translation) and not implement behavioral shortcuts. No business logic in the shim. Keep it tiny.
Jin: Also we should provide per-tenant opt-out toggles. Some enterprise customers need longer runway and contractual SLAs. That's critical for Private/Dedicated customers.
Sam: Rollout caveat: if the shim increases serialization or blocks batching, we'll see backpressure. Plan must include canary + autoscale ramp and a kill-switch.
Alex: Agreed. Minimal checklist if we run hybrid: define canonical transform spec, perf budget (target <10ms p99 added latency), per-tenant opt-outs, telemetry hooks (client-version, request-shape), docs + SDK warnings, deprecation timeline and comms cadence.
DeployBot: Deploybot scheduled canary for 6680123500. Rollback window: 2h. :robot_face:
Maria: I'll draft the RFC follow-up section with the checklist and proposed timeline. Action items: @Kevin implement shim interface and unit tests, @Sam add perf/soak tests and rollback hooks, @Jin add telemetry + rollout dashboard, @Alex own comms and deprecation notices.
Kevin: ACK — I'll open the interface PR today and include a small compatibility test harness.
Jin: I'll wire the telemetry and create a dashboard with cohort breakdowns and migration curves.
Sam: I'll add load tests and a stress scenario for batching degradation. Also will add a runbook for p99 regression.
Alex: Thanks. If anyone has strong objections to the hybrid route speak up now; otherwise I'll mark this as the chosen approach and Maria will put the follow-up in the RFC thread.
Maria: No objections from me. I'll post the follow-up RFC patch by EOD with the timeline and migration messaging.
Kevin: Quick question — can we include a snippet in the shim README showing the canonical transform? Suggest a minimal example:
```
# shim transform pseudocode
def transform(request):
    if request.headers.get('X-Old-Envelope'):
        body = unwrap_old_envelope(request.body)
        request.headers['X-Compat-Client'] = 'old'
    return request
```
Jin: Nice. That keeps expectations clear. Also include protobuf examples for typed payloads.
Alex: Cool. I'll close this thread after Maria publishes the RFC patch. Thanks folks.
Sam: :thumbsup:
DeployBot: Canary queued. Notifying infra channels.
